records.claim: The measurements were not stable because the receiver switched from lock-in mode to hold-over mode rapidly due to the low signal power.

From the tabulated results in Table 2, the mean difference of 1 PPS for the first-hour lock-in mode showed $0.00378~\mu \mathrm{s}$ after changing the mode of hold-over and a shift of $0.225\rightarrow 0.767~\mu \mathrm{s}$ in the 1PPS measurements for the first $5\mathrm{min}$ .

From the tabulated results in Table 2, the mean difference of 1 PPS for the first-hour lock-in mode showed $0.00378~\mu \mathrm{s}$ after changing the mode of hold-over and a shift of $0.225\rightarrow 0.767~\mu \mathrm{s}$ in the 1PPS measurements for the first $5\mathrm{min}$ .

records.claim: For few developed receivers, internal clock system has synchronized RecT with external PPS before operating like TtP = 0, so the receiver delay is not related with TtP.

records.claim: Most commercial receivers do not manage TtP, meaning RecT synchronizes with 10MHz reference firstly and steers to PPS input secondly, causing RecT to correspond to change through TtP changing.
records.quote: However, most of the commercial receivers do not manage TtP, which means RecT synchronizes with $10\mathrm{MHz}$ reference firstly and steers to PPS input secondly. Consequently, RecT will correspond to change through TtP changing, shown as Figure 10b.

records.claim: In the case of continuous operation, RecT is monotone changing as TtP variation, which does not adjust clock-bias after successful positioning.
records.quote: In the case of continuous operation, RecT is monotone changing as TtP variation, which does not adjust clock-bias after successful positioning.

records.claim: In the case of on-off operation, once the clock-bias exceeds adjustment threshold, the restarted receiver has to adjust clock-bias over again, which will keep RecT with the previous cycle of 10MHz phase until clock-bias less than adjustment threshold, making RecT periodic changing as TtP changing.
records.quote: In the case of on-off operation, once the clock-bias exceeds adjustment threshold, the restarted receiver has to adjust clock-bias over again, which will keep RecT with the previous cycle of $10\mathrm{MHz}$ phase until clock-bias less than adjustment threshold. Thus RecT is periodic changing as TtP changing.

records.claim: The change of RecT will directly affect the measurement pseudorange from the receiver, which impacts on calibration result of channel delay.
records.quote: Whichever continuous operation or on-off operation, the change of RecT will directly affect the measurement pseudorange from the receiver, which impacts on calibration result of channel delay.

records.claim: The receiver delay commonly refers to the time bias from radio frequency (RF) signal input to measurement data output.
records.quote: The receiver delay commonly refers to the time bias from radio frequency (RF) signal input to measurement data output.

records.claim: For the timing receiver, the timing receiver delay can be defined as the time bias from RF signal input to PPS output.
records.quote: For the timing receiver, there is also PPS output which always synchronizes with the measurement data, in other words, the timing receiver delay can be defined as the time bias from RF signal input to PPS output [10,19].

records.claim: GNSS receiver delay is divided into two parts: the channel delay existing in pseudorange and the PPS output delay caused by hardware link.
records.quote: Therefore, we divide GNSS receiver delay into two parts as shown in Figure 2. One is the channel delay existing in pseudorange, the other is PPS output delay caused by hardware link.

records.claim: EVM can be equivalently useful as signal to noise ratio and bit error rate
records.quote: We also compare among the different performance metrics and show that EVM can be equivalently useful as signal to noise ratio and bit error rate.

records.claim: EVM expresses the difference between the expected complex voltage of a demodulated symbol and the value of the actual received symbol.
records.quote: EVM expresses the difference between the expected complex voltage of a demodulated symbol and the value of the actual received symbol.

records.claim: Compared to BER, EVM is more of a measure of errors between the measured symbols and expected symbols.
records.quote: Compared to the bit error rate (BER), which gives a simple one-to-one binary decision as to whether a bit is erroneous or not, EVM is more of a measure of errors between the measured symbols and expected symbols.

records.claim: For BER measurement, the signal must be demodulated first at the receiver side.
records.quote: However, for BER measurement, it is incumbent that signal must be demodulated first at the receiver side.

records.claim: For adaptive systems like MBER based adaptive modulation systems, every update in the adaptive algorithm requires feedback from the receiver end for BER measurement.
records.scope_ref: minimum bit error rate (MBER) based adaptive modulation systems
records.quote: For many of today's adaptive systems, viz. minimum bit error rate (MBER) based adaptive modulation systems etc., this means that for every update in the adaptive algorithm, it has to receive feedback from the receiver end

records.claim: EVM can give the desired performance metric before the demodulation can actually takes place.
records.quote: In this paper, we show that for such systems, it is not always necessary to gather feedback from received end; rather EVM can give the desired performance metric before the demodulation can actually takes place.

records.claim: BER is a direct consequence of EVM.
records.quote: This can be done without any major change of algorithm in adaptive systems, since BER is a direct consequence of EVM.

records.claim: BER can be shown as a direct function of the EVM.
records.quote: The novelty in this paper lies in that the BER can be shown as a direct function of the EVM and as such in order to find equivalent performance metric, EVM can be often more useful.

records.claim: Pilots and training bits are always BPSK modulated.

contributions: propose a communication-efficient pre-training framework, DEPT
decouples embeddings from the transformer body while simultaneously training the latter on multiple data sources without requiring a shared vocabulary
train robustly and effectively under significant data heterogeneity
minimize token embedding parameters to only what the data source vocabulary requires, while cutting communication costs
enhance transformer body plasticity and generalization, improving both average perplexity and downstream task performance
enable training with custom optimized vocabularies per data source

records.claim: Magneto is a framework that combines SLMs and LLMs to derive cost-effective and general schema matching solutions.

records.claim: Magneto is structured in two phases: candidate retrieval selects a subset of the possible matches; and reranker, which ranks the candidates to make it easier for users to examine and select matches.

records.claim: Magneto leverages LLMs to automate SLMs fine-tuning by using LLMs to derive data, adding syntactic diversity and capturing different representations for column names and their values, instead of relying on manually created training data and structure-based augmentation.

Using LLMs, we can add syntactic diversity and capture different representations for column names and their values.

records.claim: Magneto addresses the challenge of high costs by using cheaper SLM-based methods for finding candidates, thereby reducing the number of matches that need to be checked by more costly LLM-based rerankers.

records.claim: Magneto variants strike a balance across runtime and accuracy dimensions and have the advantage of requiring no training data, whereas traditional methods tend to cluster at relatively high accuracy with long runtimes or relatively low runtimes with reduced accuracy.

In an active learning loop, we further add to 𝐒 a small number of posts labeled by an oracle (annotation effort) under the target-domain definition from a large unlabeled target-domain dataset 𝐓 . We use a sentence encoder to project the textual posts from 𝐒 and unlabeled query 𝐐 to the same embedding space. We use a cosine similarity metric to select the class-balanced shots most similar to 𝐐 . The text of the selected shots, their labels, and the labeling definitions (corresponding to the original labeling dimension) are used to fill in an instruction template 𝐩 , and finally passed to the pre-trained LM to make a prediction based on the conditional token probability for each class. The novelty of our method stems from: 1) populating the support set 𝐒 with a mixture of source and target domain posts, and 2) communicating the original labeling definitions as part of an instruction template 𝐩 to allow the model to relate the two.

Comparison between transfer and no-transfer scenarios across the target domain annotation sizes split by positive (#MeToo “Sexually Explicit”) and negative (#MeToo “Toxicity”) transfer scenarios. We can see that in the positive transfer scenario, the gain from transfer occurs at ever annotation size, but seem optimal with as few as 100 annotated target samples after which id diminishes.

Impact of target domain annotation size on the proportion of target examples selected as shots for few-shot prompts. We can see that this proportion increases as target domain examples are more likely to be picked as shot by semantic similarity metric.

The overall distinctness of the set $I$ is calculated as the mean of all pairwise distinctness scores:

$$

$$

$$

figures_tables.caption: The speech amplitude envelope provides a linear representation of AM fluctuations over time. Acoustic stimuli are constructed of multiple temporal dimensions [31], and modulation energy varies based upon the selected band of carrier frequencies in the signal [35]. Speech can be portrayed through a hierarchical series of AM frequency scales [43]; that is, stress placement occurs at a rate of ~ 2Hz [44], syllable rate occurs around 3 - 5Hz [24], and phonemic structure has a faster rate of 8 - 50Hz [31] (see Figure 2). Liss et al. [45] found that energy in the frequency bands below 4Hz was intercorrelated, and energy above 4Hz (up to 10Hz ) was separately intercorrelated. The frequency range between 4 and 16Hz primarily affects speech intelligibility [46], while frequencies below 4Hz strictly reflect prosodic variations, such as stress and syllable rate [47]. These multiple timescales of modulation energy within the speech envelope have been shown to elicit corresponding modulations in cortical activity during speech processing [48]. This correspondence appears to play a role in potentially challenging listening situations, such as: speech in noise [49], multiple speakers [50], complex auditory scenes [51], conflicting visual information [52], and divided attention [53,54]. Each of these situations (discussed in more detail later) requires the listener to exploit the natural timing of speech using prosodic cues, which are provided in the amplitude envelope [55].

card._title_used: neural dynamics of the processing of speech features: evidence for a progression of features from acoustic to sentential processing

records.claim: Lower-level linguistic processing, such as detection of stress and syllable segmentation, occurs in lower frequencies (< 4 Hz).
records.quote: lower-level linguistic processing, such as detection of stress and syllable segmentation, occurs in lower frequencies $(< 4\mathrm{Hz})$ [47]

records.claim: Semantic/syntactic processing may occur in higher frequencies (13 - 50 Hz).
records.quote: semantic/syntactic processing may occur in higher frequencies $(13 - 50\mathrm{Hz})$ [56]

records.claim: Traditional EEG approaches to prosody perception do not provide a comprehensive measure of how the brain tracks and encodes the multidimensional aspects of prosody over time.
records.quote: While these techniques are important for determining brain responses to prosodic features, they do not provide a comprehensive measure of how the brain tracks and encodes the multidimensional aspects of prosody over time.

records.claim: The left hemisphere favors rapid temporal features of speech, and the right hemisphere tracks slower features.
records.quote: such that the left hemisphere favors rapid temporal features of speech, and the right hemisphere tracks slower features.

records.claim: The right hemisphere generally shows stronger tracking of the speech envelope.
records.quote: The right hemisphere generally shows stronger tracking of the speech envelope [68,69]

records.claim: Envelope tracking has also been shown to be a bilateral process.
records.quote: however, envelope tracking has also been shown to be a bilateral process [62,70]

records.claim: Temporal smearing from averaging across time points will create noise in the correlation function when using simple cross-correlation between envelope and neural response.
records.quote: one issue with a simple cross-correlation between envelope and neural response is that temporal smearing (from averaging across time points) will create noise in the correlation function [71]

records.claim: The temporal response function (TRF) describes the linear mapping between stimulus and response.
records.quote: A solution to this is to use a modeling approach, known as a temporal response function (TRF) [68], to describe the linear mapping between stimulus and response.

records.claim: Forward modeling describes the mapping of a speech stimulus to a neural network using a TRF that represents the linear transformation that generated the observed neural signal.
records.quote: Forward modeling describes the mapping of a speech stimulus to a neural network [68,75,76] using a TRF that represents the linear transformation that generated the observed neural signal [77]

records.claim: The multivariate temporal response function (mTRF) uses the spectrogram representation to evaluate speech encoding.
records.quote: the forward modeling procedure may benefit from a multivariate temporal response function (mTRF) [71], which uses the spectrogram representation to evaluate speech encoding.

records.claim: Backward modeling is a mathematical representation of the linear mapping from the multivariate neural response back to the stimulus.
records.quote: Backward modeling is a mathematical representation of the linear mapping from the multivariate neural response back to the stimulus [71]

records.claim: In the backward direction, recording channels are weighted based on the information that they provide for the reconstruction, which removes inter-channel redundancies.
records.quote: In the backward direction, recording channels are weighted based on the information that they provide for the reconstruction [77], which removes inter-channel redundancies

records.claim: Measuring neural entrainment to the speech envelope is an excellent way to target prosodic processing, yet this has been underutilized in the literature.
records.scope_ref: neural entrainment to the speech envelope
records.quote: measuring neural entrainment to the speech envelope is an excellent way to target prosodic processing, yet this has been underutilized in the literature.

records.claim: cortical oscillations in the theta (4 - 7Hz) band are more closely phase-locked to intelligible speech than to unintelligible noise-vocoded speech
records.quote: Peelle et al. [32] compared intelligible speech with unintelligible noise-vocoded speech, and they found that cortical oscillations in the theta $(4 - 7\mathrm{Hz})$ band are more closely phase-locked to intelligible speech.

records.claim: envelope entrainment occurs even when speech rate is compressed to an unintelligible degree
records.quote: Nourski et al. [81] found envelope entrainment even when speech rate was compressed to an unintelligible degree

records.claim: envelope entrainment occurs to time-reversed speech stimuli
records.quote: Howard and Poeppel [82] found envelope entrainment to time-reversed speech stimuli

records.claim: envelope entrainment occurs to pseudo-word utterances
records.quote: Mai et al. [56] found envelope entrainment to pseudo-word utterances.

records.claim: it is difficult to say whether intelligibility predicts entrainment or vice versa
records.quote: given the conflicting results described here, it is difficult to say whether intelligibility predicts entrainment or vice versa.

records.claim: acoustic features of the stimulus—such as suprasegmental cues—seem to contribute to the neural entrainment effect
records.quote: What we can take away from these findings is that acoustic features of the stimulus—such as suprasegmental cues—seem to contribute to the neural entrainment effect

records.claim: selective attention in a multi-speaker environment can be observed by the degree to which neural oscillations entrain to a given speech envelope
records.quote: selective attention in a multi-speaker environment can be observed by the degree to which neural oscillations entrain to a given speech envelope [54,61,83].

records.claim: when a listener hears two speakers simultaneously, the neural decoding process is able to reconstruct the stimulus envelopes of both speech streams
records.quote: Ding and Simon [54] demonstrated that when a listener hears two speakers simultaneously, the neural decoding process is able to reconstruct the stimulus envelopes of both speech streams.

records.claim: the stimulus reconstruction is more strongly correlated to the envelope of the attended speaker
records.quote: The stimulus reconstruction is more strongly correlated to the envelope of the attended speaker (also [61,62,83]).

records.claim: neural encoding of an auditory scene involves selective phase-locking to specific auditory objects that are presented concurrently in a single auditory mixture
records.quote: these studies have suggested that neural encoding of an auditory scene involves selective phase-locking to specific auditory objects that are presented concurrently in a single auditory mixture.

records.claim: prosody likely plays an important role in multi-speaker envelope entrainment
records.quote: prosody likely plays an important role in multi-speaker envelope entrainment

records.claim: manipulations of the prosodic features of speech are rarely included as a variable in multi-speaker entrainment studies
records.quote: manipulations of the prosodic features of speech are rarely included as a variable in multi-speaker entrainment studies.

records.claim: Visual rhythmic movements help parse syllabic boundaries
records.quote: Visual rhythmic movements help parse syllabic boundaries [90]

records.claim: a wider mouth opening indicates louder amplitude
records.quote: a wider mouth opening indicates louder amplitude [91]

records.claim: seeing a conversational partner assists in segregating a speech stream from overlapping speakers
records.quote: seeing a conversational partner assists in segregating a speech stream from overlapping speakers [92].

records.claim: When auditory and visual information are incongruous, speech perception may be hindered and even lead the listener to falsely perceive a sound that was not presented in either modality
records.quote: When auditory and visual information are incongruous, speech perception may be hindered and even lead the listener to falsely perceive a sound that was not presented in either modality

records.claim: Congruent audiovisual speech enhances envelope tracking compared to incongruent information
records.quote: Congruent audiovisual speech enhances envelope tracking compared to incongruent information

records.claim: Congruent audiovisual speech shows greater envelope encoding than auditory only speech, visual only speech, or the combination of the two unisensory modalities
records.quote: Congruent audiovisual speech enhances envelope tracking compared to incongruent information and also shows greater envelope encoding than auditory only speech, visual only speech, or thecombination of the two unisensory modalities [97].

records.claim: Audiovisual speech has marked benefits for neural tracking when presented in noisy conditions
records.quote: Audiovisual speech also has marked benefits for neural tracking when presented in noisy conditions [98]

records.claim: cortical oscillations entrain to salient lip movements even when they are incongruous to the acoustic stream
records.quote: there appears to be a similar mechanism for visual entrainment in which cortical oscillations entrain to salient lip movements even when they are incongruous to the acoustic stream [101].

records.claim: Envelope entrainment is influenced by speech rhythm
records.quote: Envelope entrainment is influenced by speech rhythm [103].

records.claim: entrainment to music leads to increased timing precision in the auditory system, which leads to increased perception of the timing of speech sounds
records.quote: Some have hypothesized that entrainment to music leads to increased timing precision in the auditory system, which leads to increased perception of the timing of speech sounds [108,109].

records.claim: the accuracy of cortical entrainment to musical stimuli is contingent upon musical expertise
records.quote: Doelling and Poeppel [110] found that the accuracy of cortical entrainment to musical stimuli is contingent upon musical expertise

records.claim: musical expertise does not necessarily predict stronger entrainment to the speech envelope
records.quote: However, musical expertise does not necessarily predict stronger entrainment to the speech envelope [111].

records.claim: Temporal response function (TRF) analysis provides strong neural evidence for the emergent features of speech processing in cortex, from acoustics to higher-level linguistics, as incremental steps in neural speech processing.
records.quote: Temporal response function (TRF) analysis provides strong neural evidence for the emergent features of speech processing in cortex, from acoustics to higher-level linguistics, as incremental steps in neural speech processing.

records.claim: There is a stepwise hierarchical progression of progressively higher order features over time, reflected in both bottom-up (early) and top-down (late) processing stages.
records.quote: Critically, we show a stepwise hierarchical progression of progressively higher order features over time, reflected in both bottom-up (early) and top-down (late) processing stages.

records.claim: Linguistically driven top-down mechanisms take the form of late N400-like responses, suggesting a central role of predictive coding mechanisms at multiple levels.
records.quote: Linguistically driven top-down mechanisms take the form of late N400-like responses, suggesting a central role of predictive coding mechanisms at multiple levels.

records.claim: The neural processing of lower-level acoustic feature responses is bilateral or right lateralized, with left lateralization emerging only for lexical-semantic features.
records.quote: As expected, the neural processing of lower-level acoustic feature responses is bilateral or right lateralized, with left lateralization emerging only for lexical-semantic features.

records.claim: Removing prosodic cues from speech weakens envelope entrainment, suggesting synchrony reflects perception of acoustic manifestations of prosody.
records.quote: Ding et al. [118] have shown that removing prosodic cues from speech weakens envelope entrainment, which suggests that synchrony between neural oscillations and the speech envelope reflects perception of the acoustic manifestations of prosody

records.claim: Removing prosodic cues from connected speech stimuli still results in some low-frequency entrainment (< 10 Hz), attributed to syntactic processing.
records.quote: When Ding and colleagues [118,153] removed prosodic cues from connected speech stimuli, they did find some low-frequency entrainment $(< 10\mathrm{Hz})$ , which they attribute to syntactic processing.

records.claim: Prosodic fluctuations alone cannot fully explain neural entrainment to speech or speech comprehension.
records.quote: Of course, prosodic fluctuations alone cannot fully explain neural entrainment to speech or speech comprehension [34].

records.claim: In spoken English, syntax can exist without prosody, but the inclusion of prosody facilitates syntactic processing.
records.quote: In spoken English, syntax can exist without prosody, but the inclusion of prosody certainly facilitates syntactic processing (with phrase segmentation, pitch inflection, etc.).

records.claim: Features of prosody are directly linked to emotional expressiveness in speech.
records.quote: For example, it has been shown that features of prosody are directly linked to emotional expressiveness in speech [6]

records.claim: Patients with Parkinson's disease, aphasia, and blindness show difficulty with prosodic cues in speech.
records.scope_ref: patients with Parkinson's disease, aphasia, and blindness
records.quote: Because these populations show difficulty with prosodic cues in speech, a next step could be to examine speech envelope entrainment in these individuals to examine if there is a neural deficit in prosody encoding.

records.claim: The temporal response function (TRF) is a continuous signal exhibiting neural encoding of speech features over time, where peaks of different latencies indicate separate processing stages.
records.quote: Analogous to event related potentials (ERPs), the TRF is a continuous signal which exhibits the neural encoding of speech feature over time (typically over hundreds of milliseconds), where peaks of different latencies indicate separate processing stages.

records.claim: Many speech features require more than one stage of processing: early processing which is primarily bottom-up, and late processing which is primarily top-down.
records.quote: Our findings support these hypotheses but additionally find that many speech features require more than one stage of processing: early processing which is primarily bottom-up, and late processing which is primarily top-down

records.quote: although the LDA model can generate topics well by the probability distribution of words, it cannot give an optimal judgment about the number of topics to be selected.

records.claim: Perplexity method considers that a good topic classification model should be able to effectively classify unknown documents outside the training set
records.quote: the perplexity method considers that a good topic classification model should be able to effectively classify unknown documents outside the training set.

records.claim: JS divergence approach considers that the less similar the content among the topics classified, the better the topic classification model
records.quote: The JS divergence or JS divergence approach considers that the less similar the content among the topics classified, the better the topic classification model.

records.claim: Coherence method and stability method proposed by Greene judge the goodness of the topic classification by the similarity of the words within the same topic in the model
records.quote: Both the coherence method and the stability method proposed by Greene judge the goodness of the topic classification by the similarity of the words within the same topic in the model.

records.claim: Existing topic selection methods are not comprehensive for topic classification
records.quote: Although these existing topic selection methods are not comprehensive for topic classification, they also provide a good basis for us to think about how to judge whether a topic classification model is good or not.

records.claim: A better topic selection model should have predictive ability, isolation between topics, correct words within topics, and robustness
records.quote: Based on the existing studies, it is known that a better topic selection model should have the following characteristics: (1) The topic model has certain predictive ability; i.e., the model can classify the unknown input corpus well. (2) There should be a certain degree of isolation between different topics generated by the model; i.e., the occurrence of duplicate topics is avoided. (3) The words within each topic generated by the topic model are correct. (4) The generated model is robust; i.e., the data from the same source consistently generated similar solutions.

records.claim: There is no research to select the number of topics for LDA models from a comprehensive perspective
records.quote: There is no research to select the number of topics for LDA models from a comprehensive perspective, and most of the existing methods are one-time tests, which make it difficult to ensure that the models can be reliably and stably implemented repeatedly.

records.claim: The signal is adaptively decomposed into intrinsic mode functions (IMF) and a residue by the EMD method.
records.quote: To a given signal, firstly, it is adaptively decomposed into a set of complete and almost orthogonal components named intrinsic mode functions (IMF) by EMD method, and a residue and a collection of n IMFs, named are obtained.

records.claim: The signal can be exactly reconstructed by a linear superposition of intrinsic mode functions and a residue.
records.quote: Furthermore the signal can be exactly reconstructed by a linear superposition: $$ x (t) = \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} c _ {i} (t) + r _ {n} (t) \tag {4} $$

records.claim: The Hilbert transform is applied to each intrinsic mode function (IMF) component.
records.quote: Having obtained the IMFs, one applies the Hilbert transform to each IMF component, $$ H \left[ c _ {i} (t) \right] = \frac {1}{\pi} \int_ {- \infty} ^ {\infty} \frac {c _ {i} (\tau)}{t - \tau} \mathrm {d} \tau \tag {5} $$

records.claim: Instantaneous frequency and amplitude are computed after the Hilbert transform.
records.quote: After the Hilbert transform and together form a complex signal, and compute the instantaneous frequency and amplitude according to $$ a _ {i} (t) = \sqrt {c _ {i} ^ {2} (t) + \left(H \left[ c _ {i} (t) \right]\right) ^ {2}}, \Phi_ {i} (t) = \arctan \frac {H \left[ c _ {i} (t) \right]}{c _ {i} (t)}, \omega_ {i} (t) = \frac {\mathrm {d} \Phi_ {i} (t)}{\mathrm {d} t} \tag {6} $$

records.claim: The original signal is written as the real part of the sum of amplitude and exponential of the integral of instantaneous frequency, designated as the Hilbert-Huang spectrum.
records.quote: Finally, the original signal can be written as $$ x (t) = \operatorname {R e} \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {n} a _ {i} (t) \exp (i \int \omega_ {i} (t) d t) \tag {7} $$ Where the residue $r_n(t)$ has been left out, $\operatorname{Re}\{\cdot\}$ denotes the real part of a complex quantity. Equation(7) is designated as the Hilbert-Huang spectrum, $H(\omega, t)$ .

records.claim: The fixed-length clause model of k-CNF formulas exhibits a phase transition where formulas are almost surely satisfiable if m/n < ρ_l(k) and almost surely unsatisfiable if m/n > ρ_u(k).
records.quote: For that model it is known that there are reals ρ l ( k ) \rho_{l}(k) and ρ u ( k ) \rho_{u}(k) such that if m / n ρ l ( k ) m/n \rho_{l}(k) , a formula from the model is almost surely satisfiable (SAT), and if m / n ρ u ( k ) m/n \rho_{u}(k) , almost surely unsatisfiable (UNSAT).

records.claim: It is conjectured that ρ_l(k) = ρ_u(k), which holds asymptotically as k approaches infinity.
records.quote: It is conjectured that ρ l ( k ) = ρ u ( k ) \rho_{l}(k)=\rho_{u}(k) . That conjecture is still open. However, it holds asymptotically, i.e., the two bounds converge to each other with k → ∞ k\rightarrow\infty [ 2 ] .

records.claim: For k=3, the lower bound ρ_l(3) is at least 3.52 and the upper bound ρ_u(3) is at most 4.49, with the experimental phase transition ratio m/n close to 4.26.
records.quote: For the best studied case of k = 3 k=3 , we have ρ l ( 3 ) ≥ 3.52 \rho_{l}(3)\geq 3.52 [ 28 ] and ρ u ( 3 ) ≤ 4.49 \rho_{u}(3)\leq 4.49 [ 17 ] , and experiments show that the phase transition ratio m / n m/n is close to 4.26 4.26 [ 14 ] .

records.claim: Instances from the phase transition region are hard, while those from regions on both sides are easy, a property known as the easy-hard-easy pattern.
records.quote: Important for the solver design and testing is that instances from the phase transition region are hard and those from regions on both sides of the phase transition are easy, a property called the easy-hard-easy pattern [ 33 ] or, more accurately, the “easy-hard-less hard” pattern [ 13 ] .

records.claim: SAT solvers designed for random formulas are usually not effective on real-world instances, and vice versa, often attributed to hidden structure in industrial problems.
records.quote: Empirical studies suggest that SAT solvers devised for solving random formulas are usually not effective with real world instances; vice versa solvers for industrial instances are less efficient on random formulas [ 27 ] . This is often attributed to some form of (hidden) structure present in industrial problems that solvers designed for industrial applications can exploit [ 6 ] .

records.claim: Ansotegui et al. presented the first model where instances, despite randomness, are better solved by solvers tuned to industrial applications.
records.quote: Ansotegui et al. [ 5 ] presented the first model that may have this property: despite the “randomness” of its instances, they are better solved by solvers tuned to industrial applications.

records.claim: Giráldez-Cru and Levy proposed a model of random SAT based on modularity, showing that formulas with high modularity behave similarly to industrial ones.
records.quote: More recently, Giráldez-Cru and Levy [ 24 ] proposed a model of random SAT based on the notion of modularity , and showed that formulas with high modularity behave similarly to industrial ones.
The fixed-length clause model was extended to QBFs by Chen and Interian [ 12 ] .

records.claim: The Chen-Interian model includes parameters controlling formula structure, and exhibits a phase transition region and easy-hard-easy pattern similar to the k-CNF model.
records.quote: In addition to n n and m m (understood as above), their model includes parameters controlling the structure of formulas. Once these parameters are fixed, similar properties as in the case of the k k -CNF model emerge. There is a phase transition region associated with a specific value of the ratio m / n m/n (that does not depend on n n ) and the easy-hard-easy pattern can be experimentally verified.

records.claim: The fixed-shape model uses fixed shape and size non-normal form formulas as building blocks instead of k-clauses, and exhibits phase-transition and easy-hard-easy patterns.
records.quote: The model is similar to that of the k k -CNF one (or its extensions to QBFs), but fixed shape (and size) non-normal form formulas are used in place of k k -clauses as the key building blocks. Experimental studies again show the phase-transition and the easy-hard-easy pattern.

records.claim: Previous results on random logic programs are limited to non-disjunctive logic programs, and no models for disjunctive logic programs have been proposed so far.
records.quote: Those results are limited to non-disjunctive logic programs. No models for disjunctive logic programs have been proposed so far.

records.claim: The controlled model is a version of the Chen-Interian model where CNF matrices are subject to additional conditions restricting their structure.
records.quote: First, we propose a controlled version of the Chen-Interian model in which CNF formulas that are used as matrices are subject to additional conditions restricting their structure.

records.claim: In multi-component models, propositional formulas and QBF matrices are disjunctions of t k-CNF formulas, which are not from the fixed-shape model because their building blocks do not have a fixed size.
records.quote: In the multi-component models, propositional formulas and matrices of QBFs are disjunctions of t t k k -CNF formulas (either standard or “controlled”). They are not formulas from the fixed-shape model of Navarro and Voronkov, as their building blocks (CNF or DNF formulas) do not have a fixed size.

records.claim: The controlled model can generate formulas that are significantly harder than the corresponding Chen-Interian model.
records.quote: We compare the hardness of the controlled model with the corresponding Chen-Interian model and find that the former can generate formulas that are significantly harder.

records.claim: The multi-component model allows controlling hardness such that raising t may result in instances that are orders of magnitude harder to evaluate, even when the number of variables is fixed.
records.quote: The results show that the multi-component model allows for controlling hardness of formulas and programs in such a way that, even when the number of variables is fixed, raising t t may result in instances that are orders of magnitude harder to evaluate.

records.claim: The combination of controlled and multi-component model allows generating instances that are “super-hard” to evaluate.
records.quote: Moreover, we show that the combination of controlled and multi-component model allows to generate instances that are “super-hard” to evaluate.

records.claim: Existing detection methods frequently rely on metrics like AUROC, which require selecting optimal thresholds based on external, domain-specific calibration datasets.
records.quote: Existing detection methods (Mitchell et al., 2023a; Bao et al., 2024) frequently rely on metrics like AUROC, which, while theoretically informative, require selecting optimal thresholds based on external, domain-specific calibration datasets.

records.claim: In practical scenarios, external calibration datasets are often unavailable, significantly limiting the applicability and scalability of methods relying on them.
records.quote: In practical scenarios, such datasets are often unavailable, significantly limiting these methods' applicability and scalability.

records.claim: The proposed method employs a threshold-free aggregation strategy, eliminating dependency on external calibration sets.
records.quote: In contrast, our proposed method uniquely employs a threshold-free aggregation strategy, eliminating dependency on external calibration sets, thereby making Accuracy an inherently more practical and relevant metric for evaluation.

records.claim: AUROC quantifies the probability that a randomly selected AI-generated text receives a higher predicted probability of being machine-generated compared to a randomly chosen human-written text.
records.quote: AUROC provides a comprehensive measure of detection performance across all possible thresholds, quantifying the probability that a randomly selected AI-generated text receives a higher predicted probability of being machine-generated compared to a randomly chosen human-written text.

records.claim: Recent studies highlight that generative LLMs produce inherently skewed and poorly calibrated probability distributions, limiting the utility of AUROC for prompt-based LLM classifiers.
records.quote: However, recent studies have emphasized the limitations of AUROC for evaluating prompt-based LLM classifiers, highlighting the inherently skewed and poorly calibrated probability distributions produced by generative LLMs (Giovannotti and Gammerman, 2024; Jiang et al., 2023; Yoon et al., 2025).

records.claim: Prompt-based methods typically yield discrete predictions and uncalibrated confidence scores, rendering direct AUROC comparisons with traditional discriminative classifiers intrinsically disadvantageous and potentially misleading.
records.quote: Prompt-based methods typically yield discrete predictions and uncalibrated confidence scores, rendering direct AUROC comparisons with traditional discriminative classifiers intrinsically disadvantageous and potentially misleading (Zhang et al., 2024).

records.claim: Proficiency self-assessment (PSA) is the ability of a robot to predict, estimate, or measure how well it can perform a task in a given context and environment.
records.quote: Proficiency self-assessment (PSA) is the ability of a robot to predict, estimate, or measure how well it can perform a task in a given context and environment.

records.claim: Task-based proficiency is determined by four factors: (1) the probability and extent to which the robot will accomplish the task, (2) within a time bound or throughout a time period, (3) given a set of environmental variations, and (4) relative to contextual standards.
records.quote: the extent to which a given robot, and its sensors, actuators, and computational resources, is proficient at a task is determined by four factors: (1) the probability and extent to which the robot will accomplish the task (i.e. , achieve the task goal or set of task goals), (2) within a time bound or throughout a time period, (3) given a set of environmental variations, and (4) relative to contextual standards.

records.claim: Proficiency assessment is the ability to accurately make assertions about a robot's proficiency given the task, the context, and the robot's observations about and behaviors within the world, relative to contextual proficiency standards.
records.quote: Proficiency assessment is the ability to accurately make assertions about a robot's proficiency given the task, the context, and the robot's observations about and behaviors within the world, relative to contextual proficiency standards.

records.claim: Assessment can be performed at multiple temporal phases: a priori (before the task is executed), in situ (while the robot is performing its task or mission), or post hoc (after the mission terminates).
records.quote: Assessment can be performed at multiple temporal phases: a priori (before the task is executed), in situ (while the robot is performing its task or mission), or post hoc (after the mission terminates).

records.claim: A priori assessment enables performance predictions; in situ assessment enables adaptation to changes or transformation to new goals or operational envelopes; and post hoc assessment leads to evaluations that can inform future behaviors and longer-term learning.
records.quote: A priori assessment enables performance predictions; in situ assessment enables adaptation to changes or transformation to new goals or operational envelopes [4, 9, 69]; and post hoc assessment leads to evaluations that can inform future behaviors and longer-term learning.

records.claim: The metrics in this article apply not only to human-robot dyads but also to teams with multiple human or artificial partners.
records.quote: While the rhetorical framing of a team composed of a single human and single robot is used, the metrics in this article apply not only to human-robot dyads but also to teams with multiple human or artificial partners.

records.quote: XAI emphasizes causal factors that a human can use to calibrate trust in and reliance on decisions made by an AI algorithm.

records.claim: Neither XAI nor proficiency self-assessment is a subset of the other.

records.claim: HCI and traditional design practices encourage the parallel exploration of multiple variations to help avoid fixation on a singular idea, reduce the chances of eliminating rough but innovative ideas due to premature evaluation, and make us less prone to inflated subjective appraisals by giving us an opportunity to critically assess ideas in relation to each other.
records.quote: HCI and traditional design practices encourage the parallel exploration of multiple variations to help avoid fixation on a singular idea [30, 44], to reduce the chances of eliminating rough but innovative ideas due to premature evaluation [10, 34], and to make us less prone to inflated subjective appraisals by giving us an opportunity to critically assess ideas in relation to each other [10, 89].

records.claim: When writers do not have a way to organize and work with multiple text variations, they may end up committing to ideas too early, and focusing too much on surface level edits to refine their draft.

records.quote: revision goes beyond surface level edits [23], encompassing deeper writing subprocesses such as revising and evaluating ideas [24] and meaning discovery [87].

records.claim: Experienced writers treat revision as a recursive, non-linear process and engage with the text in repeated cycles, with multiple objectives including finding the form or shape of an argument, experimenting with vocabulary and style, and going back and forth between multiple composing activities during revision.
records.quote: Experienced writers treat revision as a recursive, non-linear process [81, 87], and engage with the text in repeated cycles, with multiple objectives including finding the form or shape of an argument [87], experimenting with vocabulary and style [43], and going back and forth between multiple composing activities during revision [22].

records.claim: There has been valuable work in HCI in designing novel editing practices, such as supporting constraints and consistency in maintaining domain-specific terms across complex documents using persistent, reified text selections that allow writers to store and compare two variations.

records.quote: However, further innovation in this space is needed to design affordances for writers that support the simultaneous consideration of multiple variations during the revision process.

records.claim: Chat-based interfaces lack scaffolding for crafting prompts, which can be difficult for novice AI users.
records.quote: These interfaces are highly intuitive, and mimic conversational interactions between humans, but lack scaffolding for crafting prompts, which can be difficult for novice AI users [49, 98].

records.claim: Simple turn-taking between the writer and the AI does not provide adequate support to writers in steering the iterative output from the LLM.
records.quote: In the context of writing with AI, simple turn-taking between the writer and the AI does not provide adequate support to writers in steering the iterative output from the LLM [14].

records.claim: The linear chat-log structure of chat-based interfaces impedes parallel exploration of multiple variations in-place.
records.quote: In contrast to the non-linear nature of how revision happens in writing [23, 87], the text-variations generated using a chat-based interface are buried within linear chat-logs, impeding parallel exploration of multiple variations in-place, where the writer is editing the document.

records.claim: In-place editing interfaces offer increased flexibility over the edited content compared to chat-based interfaces by allowing users to edit individual sections of the text.
records.quote: This offers increased flexibility over the edited content compared to chat-based interfaces by allowing users to edit individual sections of the text.

records.claim: Tools like Wordcraft and CoAuthor typically overwrite previous text with new edits, obscuring the original content.
records.quote: However, these tools typically overwrite previous text with new edits, obscuring the original content.

records.claim: Saved versions in existing tools are often linear or limited to undo/redo histories, complicating the management of multiple text variations simultaneously.
records.quote: Saved versions are often linear, as seen in Google Docs, or limited to undo/redo histories, complicating the management of multiple text variations simultaneously.

In our design, we adopt an in-place editing interface in a GPT-4 powered research prototype, offering a solution to overcome challenges surrounding the management of multiple text variations in human-AI co-writing tasks.

records.claim: ABScribe contributed an ensemble of five interface elements that significantly enhance user perceptions on AI-assisted revision by supporting rapid exploration and organization of multiple writing variations without overwhelming users.
records.quote: In our work, we contributed an ensemble of five interface elements that significantly enhance user perceptions on AI-assisted revision (RQ1) by supporting rapid exploration and organization of multiple writing variations without overwhelming users (RQ2).

contributions: We investigate several approaches for designers to give feedback to UI generation models, using familiar interactions such as commenting, sketching and direct manipulation.
We first perform an evaluation with 21 designers where they gave feedback using these interactions, which resulted in ~1500 design annotations.
We then use this data to finetune a series of LLMs to generate higher quality UIs.
We evaluate these models with human judges, and we find that our designer-aligned approaches outperform models trained with traditional ranking feedback and all tested baselines, including GPT-5.
We released the dataset and models from our work.

contributions: We introduce RankArena, a unified platform for comparing and analysing the performance of retrieval pipelines, rerankers, and RAG systems

RankArena supports multiple evaluation modes: direct reranking visualisation, blind pairwise comparisons with human or LLM voting, supervised manual document annotation, and end-to-end RAG answer quality assessment
The platform also integrates LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, enabling comparison between model-generated rankings and human ground truth annotations
All interactions are stored as structured evaluation datasets that can be used to train rerankers, reward models, judgment agents, or retrieval strategy selectors

records.claim: Evaluating the quality of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and document reranking systems remains challenging due to the lack of scalable, user-centric, and multi-perspective evaluation tools.
records.quote: Evaluating the quality of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and document reranking systems remains challenging due to the lack of scalable, user-centric, and multi-perspective evaluation tools.

records.claim: RankArena is a unified platform for comparing and analysing the performance of retrieval pipelines, rerankers, and RAG systems using structured human and LLM-based feedback as well as for collecting such feedback.
records.quote: We introduce RankArena, a unified platform for comparing and analysing the performance of retrieval pipelines, rerankers, and RAG systems using structured human and LLM-based feedback as well as for collecting such feedback.

records.claim: RankArena supports multiple evaluation modes: direct reranking visualisation, blind pairwise comparisons with human or LLM voting, supervised manual document annotation, and end-to-end RAG answer quality assessment.
records.quote: RankArena supports multiple evaluation modes: direct reranking visualisation, blind pairwise comparisons with human or LLM voting, supervised manual document annotation, and end-to-end RAG answer quality assessment.

records.claim: RankArena captures fine-grained relevance feedback through both pairwise preferences and full-list annotations, along with auxiliary metadata such as movement metrics, annotation time, and quality ratings.
records.quote: It captures fine-grained relevance feedback through both pairwise preferences and full-list annotations, along with auxiliary metadata such as movement metrics, annotation time, and quality ratings.

records.claim: The platform integrates LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, enabling comparison between model-generated rankings and human ground truth annotations.
records.quote: The platform also integrates LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, enabling comparison between model-generated rankings and human ground truth annotations.

records.claim: All interactions are stored as structured evaluation datasets that can be used to train rerankers, reward models, judgment agents, or retrieval strategy selectors.
records.quote: All interactions are stored as structured evaluation datasets that can be used to train rerankers, reward models, judgment agents, or retrieval strategy selectors.

records.claim: Conventional benchmarks often relying on static datasets and predefined metrics fail to capture user-centric notions of quality such as document relevance, answer usefulness, or faithfulness in generation.
records.quote: Conventional benchmarks [42, 43] often relying on static datasets and predefined metrics fail to capture user-centric notions of quality such as document relevance, answer usefulness, or faithfulness in generation.

records.claim: RankArena is a unified, open-source evaluation and annotation platform that supports multi-faceted assessment of retrieval, reranking, and generation quality.
records.quote: To address this gap, we introduce RankArena, a unified, open-source evaluation and annotation platform that supports multi-faceted assessment of retrieval, reranking, and generation quality.

Inspired by recent efforts such as MT-Bench [9] and Chatbot Arena [15], our platform extends the evaluation paradigm beyond model-centric metrics by integrating human-in-the-loop and LLM-as-a-judge feedback [21, 47].

The functions all take the same inputs, a DataFrame and a ZenoOptions object with information such as data paths and column names. @model functions return a function for getting running model inference. In the example above, the @model function loads a speech-to-text model and returns a function that transcribes audio data. @metric functions calculate aggregate metrics on subsets of data. Above, the @metric function computes the average word error rate (avg_wer) for transcribed audio. @distill functions derive new metadata columns. Above, the @distill function calculates the amplitude value from audio. @transform functions produce new data inputs. Above, the @transform function lowers the amplitude of audio samples.

contributions: We propose human-in-the-loop adversarial generation, where human authors are guided to break models.
We aid the authors with interpretations of model predictions through an interactive user interface.
We apply this generation framework to a question answering task called Quizbowl.
The resulting questions are validated via live human-computer matches.
The adversarial questions cover diverse phenomena from multi-hop reasoning to entity type distractors.

figures_tables.caption: The topical diversity of the questions in the adversarially authored data set based on a random sample of 100 questions.
The adversarially authored questions have similar n-gram overlap to the regular test questions. However, the overlap of the named entities (NE) decreases for IR Adversarial questions.
A breakdown of the phenomena in the adversarially authored data set.

The first category of adversarially authored questions consists of examples that require reasoning. Answer displays the correct answer (all models were incorrect). For these examples, connecting the training and adversarially authored clues is simple for humans but difficult for models.

The second category of adversarial questions consists of clues that are present in the training data but are written in a distracting manner. Training shows relevant snippets from the training data. Prediction displays the RNN model's answer prediction (always correct on Training, always incorrect on Adversarial).

An example Quizbowl question. The question becomes progressively easier (for humans) to answer later on; thus, more knowledgeable players can answer after hearing fewer clues. Our adversarial writing process ensures that the clues also challenge computers.

The interpretation successfully aids an attack against the IR system. The author removes the phrase containing the words “ellipse” and “parabola”, which are highlighted in the interface (shown in bold). In its place, they add a phrase which the model associates with the answer sphere.
Failure and success cases for SCPN. The model fails to create a valid paraphrase of the sentence for 97% of questions.
A failed attempt to trick the neural model. The author modifies the question multiple times, replacing words suggested by the interpretation, but is unable to break the system.

records.quote: the amount of open-source library code has been shown to be more than $45\%$ of the total project code for open-source Java projects, with only $10\%$ of projects not reusing code at all [18].

records.claim: Of 1,546 commercial codebases analyzed in 2020, 98% contained open-source library code, with the average application being comprised of 75% open source.
records.quote: the 2021 Synposis Open Source Security Report finds that of 1,546 commercial codebases analyzed in 2020, $98\%$ contained open-source library code, with the average application being comprised of $75\%$ open source [42].

records.claim: Dependency graphs can exhibit depths larger than six, with roughly 25% of all artifacts having a dependency graph of depth at least three.
records.quote: Decan et al. have shown in 2019 that these graphs can exhibit depths larger than six, with roughly $25\%$ of all artifacts having a dependency graph of depth at least three.

records.quote: a 2017 study performed by Kula et al. found that $69\%$ of developers claim to be unaware of being affected. As a result, more than $81\%$ of the systems they analyzed contained vulnerable dependencies [20].

records.claim: One reason for developers not upgrading dependencies is the perception of security patches and dependency upgrades as added responsibility yielding little to no benefits for the user.

records.claim: The mode of operation that considers all valid releases as possible dependencies results in data that is an overapproximation of reality.
records.quote: Therefore, this mode of operation results in data that is an overapproximation $(\mathbb{M}_{>})$ of reality.

records.claim: The mode of operation that selects the most recent release of the target library yields an underapproximation of reality.
records.quote: This mode of operation yields an underapproximation $(\mathbb{M}_{<})$of reality.

records.claim: The underapproximation mode ($\mathbb{M}_{<}$) yields data that is intuitively closer to reality because package managers always select one target per dependency and only deviate from the most recent release in rare cases of version conflicts.
records.quote: However, since package managers always select one target per dependency, and only deviate from the most recent release in the rare case of version conflicts, we consider $\mathbb{M}_{<}$ to yield data that is intuitively closer to reality.

records.definition: Data resulting from a mode of operation where all valid releases of the target library are considered as possible dependencies.
records.quote: Therefore, this mode of operation results in data that is an overapproximation $(\mathbb{M}_{>})$ of reality.

records.definition: Data resulting from a mode of operation where only the most recent release of the target library is selected as the dependency.
records.quote: This mode of operation yields an underapproximation $(\mathbb{M}_{<})$of reality.

records.claim: The data model for software artifacts contains a unique library identifier, a version number, the release date, and a list of artifact dependencies.
records.quote: the set of properties for software artifacts in our data model contains a unique library identifier, a version number, the release date, and a list of artifact dependencies.

records.claim: The data model for vulnerabilities includes the vulnerability's internal Snyk identifier, its severity, a reference to an associated CVE identifier, the date of disclosure, and the date of publication.
records.quote: we define our data model for vulnerabilities, which includes the vulnerability's internal Snyk identifier, its severity (Critical, High, Medium or Low) and a reference to an associated CVE identifier, if available. Furthermore, we incorporate the date of disclosure and date of publication.

records.claim: The data model features a single entity called ArtifactReference used to model both artifact dependencies and vulnerability-to-artifact relations.
records.quote: It features a single entity called ArtifactReference, which is used to model both artifact dependencies and vulnerability-to-artifact relations.

records.claim: A Patching Relation connects each vulnerability to zero or more artifacts that incorporate the respective patch.
records.quote: A Patching Relation connects each vulnerability to zero or more artifacts that incorporate the respective patch.

records.claim: The Patch Detector finds artifacts that patch a vulnerability, defined as the first artifacts of the targeted library that are not affected by the vulnerability anymore.
records.quote: the Patch Detector then enumerates all vulnerabilities in the data set and finds those artifacts that patch the vulnerability, i.e., the first artifacts of the targeted library that are not affected by the vulnerability anymore.

records.claim: Fixed artifact references, used predominantly by Maven, specify a unique library identifier and version number to reference exactly one target artifact.
records.quote: The first one, which is used predominantly by Maven, is to specify the unique library identifier and the version number of the target artifact. We call this a fixed artifact reference, as it references exactly one target artifact.

records.claim: Version ranges in Maven are rarely used in online artifacts.
records.quote: While Maven also supports the use of version ranges [30], we find that these are rarely used in any of the artifacts online.

records.claim: Floating artifact references, used in NPM and NuGet, consist of a unique library identifier and a range of valid version numbers.
records.quote: However, floating artifact references, which are used in NPM and NuGet, consist of the unique library identifier and a range of valid version numbers.

records.claim: For floating artifact references, the build system usually selects the most recent release of the respective library.
records.quote: For this type of reference, the build system selects one of the valid target artifacts, which usually is the most recent release of the respective library.
